question: Two jobs each need 60 minutes. Worked in alternating 10-minute slices, with no switching cost at all, when is the first job finished, in minutes?
move: Juggling delays every finish line, even before any switching costs are counted.
ask: Which one task could I finish first today, instead of nudging three along at once?
trap: About 60 minutes, as if splitting time cost nothing.
hint: Count which slice in the whole sequence is the first job's last one.
steps: Each job needs 60 ÷ 10 = 6 slices, taken in turn: A, B, A, B and so on.
The first job's sixth slice is the eleventh slice overall.
reference: Pinedo, Scheduling: Theory, Algorithms, and Systems, 5th ed., Springer, 2016
